column1: # jls-ledger.tsv — every leaf section of java-langspec-1.0.pdf, with its coverage status.
# Transcribed from the spec's own table of contents (PDF pp. 7-19, printed vii-xix).
# This file is the WHOLE against which coverage is measured: a subset chosen by hand is
# indistinguishable from completeness unless the whole is written down first.
# status: COVERED | N/A | UNCOVERED    (default UNCOVERED; there is no fourth value)
#   COVERED  -> reason_or_templates lists the template ids exercising it (computed, not typed)
#   N/A      -> reason_or_templates is a written reason citing spec text or a TESTED behaviour
# Checked by conformance/check-ledger (gapless numbering, monotone pages, chapter anchoring).

column5: reason_or_templates

column6: The printed §1.1 `class Test` is a complete runnable program: `main(String[] args)` echoes its command-line arguments via System.out.print/println and must print exactly `Hello, world.`

column5: A bibliography of external documents (Dylan, CLOS, ARM, IEEE 754, Unicode); it states no rule about Java, so no program can observe it.
Defines context-free-grammar metaterminology only (production, nonterminal, terminal, alphabet, goal symbol); names no Java construct a program could exercise.

column6: White space and comments are discarded before the syntactic grammar, so a comment still separates two tokens (`a/**/b` is two identifiers, never `ab`).

column5: Document organization only: which chapters carry the syntactic grammar and how the expository form differs from the Chapter 19 LALR(1) form; no production or rule is stated here.

column6: The notation's expansions are directly compilable claims: all eight `for` forms from the `opt` subscript, both `break ;` / `break Identifier ;` forms, and `true`/`false` as BooleanLiteral rather than Identifier.
non-ASCII Unicode is legal only in comments, identifiers and character/string literal contents, where it carries its Unicode 2.0 code value
longest-possible-match tokenization: `i+++j` lexes as `i++ + j`, `a--b` as `a`,`--`,`b`
\\uxxxx is translated before tokenizing (so `A` can spell a token), multiple u's allowed, and an even/odd backslash count decides eligibility so `\\u005a` is not `Z`
CR, LF and CR LF each terminate exactly one line, ending a // comment and making an unclosed literal a compile-time error
white space or a comment between `-` and `=` prevents them forming the `-=` token, and a trailing ASCII SUB is ignored
space, HT, FF and line terminators all count as token-separating white space
comments do not nest and // has no meaning inside /*, so `/* this /* // /** ends here: */` is one comment; a comment delimiter inside a string literal is ordinary text

column5: Ch3
column6: identifiers are unlimited-length Java-letter/digit sequences including $ and _, and are the same only if every Unicode character matches (LATIN A, GREEK ALPHA, CYRILLIC A are three distinct names)

column5: Ch3
column6: the 47 reserved keywords, including the unused `const` and `goto`, are rejected as identifiers at compile time
each of the six literal kinds denotes a value whose type is the primitive type, String, or the null type it names
decimal/hex/octal forms with optional L suffix; 0x80000000 is int -2147483648 and 0xffffffff is -1, and out-of-range decimal literals are compile-time errors
f/F suffix yields float and otherwise double, with a compile-time error if a nonzero literal rounds to infinity or to zero
`true` and `false` are the two values of type boolean
a character literal is always type char and always exactly one character; ' ' is a compile-time error while '\\n' is not

column5: Ch15
column6: string literals and compile-time constant expressions are interned so `==` is true across classes, while runtime-computed strings are distinct until .intern()

column2: Escape Sequences for Character and String Literals
column6: \\b \\t \\n \\f \\r \\" \\' \\\\ map to their code points and octal escapes cover \0-ÿ (so '\\101' == 'A')
`null` is the single value of the null type and is assignable to any reference variable
the nine ASCII characters ( ) { } [ ] ; , . each lex as a single separator token
the 37 operator tokens each lex as one token, including the three-and-four character forms >>> and >>>=

column2: The Kinds of Types and Values
column6: the null reference is the only value of the null type and can be cast to any reference type (and no variable may be declared of the null type)
primitive values share no state — a primitive variable's value changes only by assignment to that variable; boolean has exactly two values and the integral/floating widths are 8/16/32/64-bit
the exact inclusive ranges of byte, short, int, long, and char (0..65535)
integer ops are 32-bit unless an operand is long (then 64-bit), overflow is silent and wraps, and / or % by zero throws ArithmeticException
IEEE 754 values: 0.0==-0.0 is true but 1.0/0.0 is +Inf and 1.0/-0.0 is -Inf, and NaN is unordered so x!=x is true exactly when x is NaN
binary float ops promote to double if either operand is double, round to nearest, produce no exceptions (overflow→signed infinity, gradual underflow, no flush-to-zero)

column2: The boolean Type and boolean Values
column6: only boolean expressions drive if/while/do/for and ?:, boolean casts only to boolean, and string conversion of a boolean yields "true"/"false"
a variable or field may be declared with a class type, an interface type, or an array type written Type[], and all three are usable
references alias: mutation of an object's state through one reference is observed through another reference to the same object
every class and array inherits Object's methods — getClass, toString, equals, hashCode, clone — and an Object variable holds any instance or array
a String's value is constant (unchanging), string literals are references to String instances, and + creates a new String

column2: When Reference Types Are the Same
column6: type identity: same fully-qualified name means the same class/interface, and two array types are the same type iff their component types are (observable via getClass() identity)
a type name is usable in each listed position — field, method parameter, method result, constructor parameter, local, catch parameter, new, array creation, cast, instanceof
a variable always holds a value assignment-compatible with its declared type, checked at compile time except the one run-time array-store check
a primitive variable holds a value of exactly its declared type, so a narrower type keeps no widened residue (e.g. byte b=(byte)200 reads back as -56)
a reference variable holds null or a reference to any object whose class is assignment compatible with the variable's type
variable creation and extent per kind: one class variable per class, one instance variable per object, and a fresh parameter/local created per invocation or per block/for entry
fields and array components are initialized to type defaults (0, 0L, 0.0f, 0.0d, '\0', false, null) before use

column2: Variables Have Types, Objects Have Classes
column6: a variable's declared type differs from the object's class: an interface-typed variable holds any implementing instance, and an array's class name is e.g. "[I"

column5: The section body is a single taxonomic sentence — "Specific type conversions in Java are divided into six categories." (p. 54) — naming the buckets its subsections define; it states no rule a program's compilation or execution can exhibit.

column6: a redundant cast to a value's own type is permitted and value-preserving, and boolean's only conversion is boolean-to-boolean
the 19 widenings never throw: signed integrals sign-extend, char zero-extends, and int/long to float/double rounds IEEE-nearest with possible precision loss (1234567890 to float loses 46)
float/double to integral rounds toward zero, NaN yields 0, out-of-range clamps to the type's MIN/MAX, integral narrowing keeps the low n bits, and none of the 23 ever throws
subclass-to-superclass, class-to-implemented-interface, null-to-any-reference, array-to-Object/Cloneable, and SC[]-to-TC[] all succeed with no run-time check
a narrowing reference conversion tests the value at run time and throws ClassCastException when the actual class is not assignment compatible
every type including the null type has a string conversion, so "" + anyValue produces a String (null yields "null")

javelinac rejects the forbidden set — reference-to-primitive, primitive-to-reference, any non-identity conversion to/from boolean, casts between unrelated class types, array to a class type other than Object/String

an int constant expression narrows implicitly to byte/short/char when representable (byte b = 42;), non-constant narrowing is a compile-time error, and assignment itself never throws except an array-element ArrayStoreException
argument conversion allows only identity/widening — the implicit constant narrowing of §5.2 is excluded, so m(12, 2) against m(byte,int)/m(short,short) is a compile-time error
string conversion fires only for binary + when one operand is a String, converting the other operand and yielding the concatenation

a reference cast checks the run-time class against the target (null always passes) and throws ClassCastException otherwise; provably impossible casts, e.g. to an unrelated class or an interface a final class lacks, are compile-time errors
promotion contexts admit only identity and widening primitive conversions, so an arithmetic operand is never narrowed
byte/short/char promote to int for array dimension and index expressions, unary +, -, and ~, and for each shift operand separately, so a long shift distance does not promote the shifted value
binary operands promote by the double > float > long > int ladder for * / %, + -, < <= > >=, == !=, & ^ |, and ?: — so char & byte computes as int & int
a constructor declaration introduces no name, so a class may also declare a method whose name is the class name
statement labels are a separate namespace: a label may reuse a local variable's identifier without hiding it
forward reference in a field initializer is a compile-time error while a constructor may use a later-declared field; type declarations need not precede use
a local variable hides a class variable; the hidden one is still reachable as Test.x (prints x=0, Test.x=1)
an inaccessible, hidden, or overridden superclass member is not inherited into the subclass's member set
same simple name in two packages denotes two distinct types (vector.Vector vs java.util.Vector); a package cannot contain a class and subpackage of one name

column2: The Members of a Class Type
column6: a field and method may share a name; a field inherited from two interfaces is ambiguous by simple name (compile-time error); overriding removes Object.toString from the member set

column2: The Members of an Interface Type
column6: an interface inheriting same-named fields from two superinterfaces makes that simple name a compile-time error (ColorsAndSeparates)

column2: The Members of an Array Type
column6: array type has Object's members plus final int length; int[] arrays of different sizes share one class (ia.getClass()==ib.getClass())

column2: Determining the Meaning of a Name
column6: a name's category comes from its context, so one identifier can denote a type, a method, and a variable in the same body

column2: Syntactic Classification of a Name According to Context
column6: context fixes the syntactic category: identifier before '(' is a MethodName, in a cast/instanceof/new is a TypeName, as assignment LHS is an ExpressionName
ambiguous-name reclassification order: local/param, then field, then type, then package (ORG.rpgpoet.Music.wizards.length resolves left-to-right)

column5: the section body is a single lead-in sentence ("determined as follows") stating no rule of its own; it has no behaviour a program could observe

column6: a simple package name naming no accessible top-level package is a compile-time error
in Q.Id, Q must name an accessible package and Id an accessible subpackage, else compile-time error

column5: the section body is a single lead-in sentence ("determined as follows") stating no rule of its own; it has no behaviour a program could observe

column6: simple type name lookup order: current compilation unit, then same package, then a single on-demand import; two on-demand imports of the name is a compile-time error
a qualified type name Q.Id must name an accessible type in package Q (java.util.Date usable without import), else compile-time error

column5: the section body is a single lead-in sentence ("determined as follows") stating no rule of its own; it has no behaviour a program could observe

column6: a simple name denotes local/param before field; a final field denotes a value so assigning to it is a compile-time error, as is naming an instance variable from a static context
Q.Id: package-qualified Q is an error, class-name Q requires a static field, and expression Q of non-reference type (i.x on an int) is a compile-time error
a MethodName may appear only in a method invocation expression, so using a method's name as a value is a compile-time error
a simple method name must name at least one method of the enclosing class or interface, else compile-time error
Q.Id(...): package-name Q is an error, type-name Q requires a static method, expression Q requires a method of Q's type (p.nPoints() on a field is an error)
access control governs qualified access, class instance creation, explicit constructor invocation, and Class.newInstance
public/protected/private/default accessibility of types and members determines whether a qualified access compiles

protected member access from another package is permitted only through super.Id or an expression whose type is S or a subclass of S; protected constructor is unusable via new T(...) outside the package
a non-public class is usable only inside its package while a public class's public methods are usable anywhere, and protected fields only in subclasses

column2: Example: Access to public and Non-public Classes
column6: a public class is reachable from another package by FQN or single-type-import; a non-public class in the same unit is not (compile-time error)

column2: Example: Default-Access Fields, Methods, and Constructors
column6: a default-access method is not inherited across packages: the subclass's same-signature move does not override, so moveAlso calls Point.move and terminates instead of recursing

column2: Example: public Fields, Methods, and Constructors
column6: public members (including a public static field) are usable from any package, while default-access fields of the same public class are not

column2: Example: protected Fields, Methods, and Constructors
column6: protected fields of a Point parameter are inaccessible in Point3d.delta but accessible in delta3d via a Point3d parameter (compile-time errors)

column2: Example: private Fields, Methods, and Constructors
column6: private members are usable only inside the declaring class body and are not inherited by subclasses
every type has a fully qualified name usable in source (java.lang.Object, points.Point, double[]), formed by package name plus simple name

column5: the section is an explicit recommendation ("We recommend these conventions... should not be followed slavishly"); a program that ignores the conventions behaves identically, so nothing is observable

column6: a field, parameter, or local declaration can hide a package name in an expression, but a type name never hides a package name in a package/import declaration

column5: purely stylistic capitalization advice plus a statistical remark that hiding "is rare"; the language does not rely on case distinctions, so no rule here changes program behaviour

column6: method names cannot hide or be hidden by other names, so a same-named variable and method coexist and each use resolves by context
a field name can hide a package or type name (recoverable via import or FQN) but can never hide a method name
a constant field name cannot hide a method name of the same spelling, since the two are distinguished syntactically

column5: only style advice on short local/parameter names (b for byte, i/j/k for ints); it states no rule, and identifier choice has no effect a program can observe

column6: a package may not contain a type declaration and a subpackage of the same simple name (compile-time error); subpackage FQN is P.Q

column5: states only that the host determines how packages/compilation units are created, stored, and made accessible — a host-environment concern with no rule a Java program can execute

column2: Storing Packages in a File System
column5: pure host/tooling: directory layout, CLASSPATH, and the @uxxxx file-name escaping convention for mapping package names to pathnames; nothing observable from inside a compiled program
describes a host storing packages in a database and which §7.6 restrictions such a host may relax — a storage/tooling choice, not a rule a Java program can exercise

column6: all three parts of a compilation unit are optional, and types in different compilation units may depend on each other circularly
a compilation unit's package membership comes from its package declaration; absent one it belongs to an unnamed package
a type T in a compilation unit declaring `package P;` has fully qualified name P.T and is referable by it
a compilation unit with no package declaration compiles and runs in the unnamed package, its types visible by simple name to that package

column2: Scope and Hiding of a Package Name
column6: package names never hide other names (a same-spelled variable/type/package coexist)

column2: Access to Members of a Package
column6: java and its subpackages lang, io, util are always accessible without any host configuration
an import's simple name is in scope only in its own compilation unit — not in other compilation units of the same package, which must use the fully qualified name
`import P.T;` makes T available as a simple name; nonexistent/non-public/non-accessible type, subpackage import, or two different types with the same simple name is a compile-time error
`import P.*;` makes all public types of P available on demand, and a single-type-import or a type declared in the compilation unit hides the on-demand name
every compilation unit implicitly imports java.lang.*, so String/Object/Math resolve with no import declaration
a single-type-import of java.util.Vector does not stop a package named Vector from being recognized in a later import; the program compiles and prints both class names
stray semicolons between type declarations are ignored, and a non-public type in a package is inaccessible from another package

column5: a reversed-domain-name convention the section itself says is "not enforced by a Java compiler" — advice about choosing identifiers, with no rule whose violation a program could detect

column6: a class declaration creates a new instantiable reference type; duplicate class/interface name in a package is a compile-time error

column2: Scope of a Class Type Name
column6: a class name's scope is the whole package, so mutually forward-referencing classes compile
repeating a class modifier (e.g. `public public class`) is a compile-time error
`new` on an abstract class is a compile-time error, but instantiating a concrete subclass runs the abstract class's constructor and field initializers
naming a final class in an extends clause is a compile-time error
a class with no extends clause has Object as direct superclass; a declared subclass cycle is a compile-time error
a non-abstract class must implement every method of its direct superinterfaces; one declaration can implement two superinterfaces' identical method
a member's scope is the entire class body, so a method may refer to a field declared textually later
private members are not inherited, and constructors are not members so a subclass does not inherit them

column5: the section body is a single sentence announcing the example subsections ("This section illustrates inheritance of class members through several examples") — it states no rule at all, so there is nothing a program can exercise

column6: a default-access field is not inherited by a subclass in another package (compile-time error on use)
public and protected fields are inherited and usable by a subclass in another package
a private static field is not inherited; a subclass referring to it is a compile-time error
an instance of a non-public class is usable through a public supertype, and its public overriding method is invoked dynamically from another package
a subclass field hides a same-named superclass field, which stays reachable via super or a cast; two fields with one name in a class body is an error
a repeated modifier, or more than one of public/protected/private, on a field declaration is a compile-time error
a static field has exactly one incarnation shared by all instances, while each instance gets its own non-static field
a final field requires an initializer and assigning to it is a compile-time error, though the referenced object's state may still change
a transient field is accepted and behaves identically to an ordinary field in program execution (the spec defers persistence to an unspecified service)
declaring a field both final and volatile is a compile-time error (the memory-model part is single-threaded-unobservable, but this rule is not)
a class-variable initializer runs once at class initialization while an instance-variable initializer runs on every instance creation; an initializer that can throw a checked exception is an error
forward reference by simple name, or use of this/super, in a class-variable initializer is a compile-time error
forward reference to another instance variable by simple name is an error, but referring to a later-declared static, or to this/super, is legal

column5: the section body is one sentence introducing its example subsections ("The following examples illustrate some (possibly subtle) points about field declarations"); it contains no rule, so there is no behaviour to observe

column6: a hiding static field is seen by simple name while super.x / Point.x sees the hidden one (prints `4.7 2`)
a field access selects the field of the reference expression's static type, so `sample.x` and `((Point)sample).x` differ (prints `4.7 2`)
referring by simple name to a field inherited from both a superclass and an interface is an ambiguity error; super.v and Frob.v disambiguate (prints 2.5)
a field inherited from one interface by several paths is inherited once and its simple name is unambiguous
two methods with the same signature in one class body is a compile-time error; a method and a field may share a name
argument values initialize freshly created parameter variables; duplicate parameter names, or redeclaring a parameter as a local, is an error
signature is name plus parameter count and types, so two same-signature declarations collide even when one is abstract
a repeated method modifier, or abstract combined with private/static/final/native, is a compile-time error
an abstract method must live in an abstract class and every concrete subclass must implement it; invoking one via super is an error
a static method is invoked without an object, and using this or super in its body is a compile-time error
overriding or hiding a final method is a compile-time error; methods of a final class and private methods are implicitly final
a native method's body must be a semicolon, and declaring a native method abstract is a compile-time error

column5: the whole section specifies lock acquisition on the Class object or on this before the method body runs, equivalent to a synchronized statement (§14.17, §17); the target is Java 1.0 minus synchronized with no threads or locks, so no program can observe the locking

column6: a checked exception thrown by a body must appear in the throws clause, and a non-Throwable type in a throws clause is an error
abstract/native methods must have a semicolon body and others a block; a value-returning method whose body can complete normally is an error
a class inherits every accessible superclass/superinterface method it does not override or hide, and can invoke it on its own instances
an overriding instance method is dispatched dynamically and reachable via super, while a cast to the superclass type does not reach the overridden one
a static method hides a same-signature superclass static method (reachable by qualified name); a static method hiding an instance method is an error
an override with a different return type, a conflicting throws clause, or reduced access is a compile-time error

column2: Inheriting Methods with the Same Signature
column6: when several same-signature methods are inherited, the non-abstract one implements the rest; a static one, or mismatched return types, is an error
overload selection uses the argument count and compile-time types, and overriding one overload leaves the sibling overload inherited

column5: the section body is one sentence introducing its example subsections ("The following examples illustrate some (possibly subtle) points about method declarations"); it states no rule, so there is nothing to exercise

column6: the overriding move is invoked even through a variable of the superclass type
a subclass can simultaneously hide the superclass fields, override move(int,int), and overload it with move(float,float)
overriding getX/getY with a float return type where the superclass returns int is a compile-time error
the program prints `(0, 0)` / `(2.7182798, 3.14159)` / `(2, 3)` / `(2, 3)`, showing fields hide but methods override

column2: Example: Invocation of Hidden Class Methods
column6: prints `Goodnight, Dick` — the hidden static method is picked by the variable's declared type, the instance method by the object's class
an inherited putstr calls the overriding putchar of the receiver, so the program prints `lbo` / `print` / `lbo`

column2: Example: Incorrect Overriding because of Throws
column6: an override declaring a checked exception the superclass method does not is an error, and so is throwing it without a throws clause
static initializers and class-variable initializers run in textual order at class initialization, so a method called from an earlier initializer sees the default value 0
a constructor runs on `new`; its name must be the class's simple name, and it is not a member so it cannot be inherited, hidden, or invoked by a method call
constructor formal parameters bind the arguments of a class instance creation expression exactly as method parameters do (duplicate parameter name is an error)
two constructors with the same parameter types in one class is a compile-time error
only public/protected/private are allowed; declaring a constructor abstract, static, final, or native is a compile-time error
a checked exception thrown by a constructor must be listed in its throws clause and handled at the creation expression

super(...) is inserted implicitly and instance-variable initializers run after it in textual order, whereas this(...) does not rerun them; constructor self-invocation cycles and instance-variable use in an explicit invocation are errors
overloaded constructors are selected at compile time by the class instance creation expression's argument types
a class with no constructors gets a no-arg default that calls super(), public exactly when the class is public; an error if the superclass has no no-arg constructor
a class whose only constructor is private cannot be instantiated from outside its own declaration
an interface declaration introduces a usable reference type; a class and an interface with the same name in one package is a compile-time error

column2: Scope of an Interface Type Name
column6: an interface type name is in scope over the whole package, so it can be used before/above its own declaration and from a sibling compilation unit
only public/abstract may precede `interface`, and a repeated modifier is a compile-time error
every interface is implicitly abstract: an explicit `abstract interface` behaves identically and no interface can be instantiated
extends transitively inherits superinterface methods/constants and makes an implementor assignable and `instanceof`-true for every superinterface; circular extends is a compile-time error
an interface body admits only constant and abstract-method members (a method body or constructor is a compile-time error), and member names scope over the entire body
interface members are implicitly public and reachable from another package exactly when the interface itself is public
an interface's members are its own plus everything inherited from direct superinterfaces except fields it hides and methods it overrides
an interface field is implicitly public static final — assignment to it is a compile-time error, and transient/volatile on it is a compile-time error

every interface field needs an initializer (need not be constant), evaluated exactly once at interface initialization; forward reference by simple name, and `this`/`super` in the initializer, are compile-time errors

column5: a single lead-in sentence ("The following example illustrates some (possibly subtle) points about field declarations") with no rule of its own; all normative content is in 9.3.2.1 and 9.3.2.2

column6: a field name inherited from two different direct superinterfaces is an ambiguous member: any simple-name use is a compile-time error
one declaration inherited by several diamond paths yields a single member, usable by simple name without ambiguity
interface methods are implicitly public abstract with a `;` body; static/native/final on them is a compile-time error, yet an implementing class method may be final or native
a subinterface method overrides the same signature per-signature; a differing return type (or return vs void) and a widening throws clause are compile-time errors
same name with different signatures overloads legally across declared and inherited interface methods, with no required return-type or throws relationship

column5: a single lead-in sentence ("The following examples illustrate some (possibly subtle) points about abstract method declarations") stating no rule; the observable content is in 9.4.3.1 and 9.4.3.2

column6: an overriding interface method may narrow the throws clause (InfiniteBuffer.get throws only BufferError), so a call through the subinterface need not handle the dropped exception
a subinterface overloading an inherited method has all three signatures; an implementing class must supply all three and calls dispatch by argument type

column5: Ch10
column6: an array whose component type is an interface or abstract class holds null or instances of any implementing/concrete-subclass type; length is not part of the array type

column5: Ch10,Ch10b
column6: declaring an array variable creates no array (stays null) while `T[] v` and `T v[]` declare the same type, and one variable can successively hold arrays of different lengths

column5: Ch10
column6: `new T[n]` and an array initializer both create an array whose `length` is a final field and whose every component is initialized

column5: Ch10
column6: array access is 0-origin with byte/short/char indices promoted to int, and an index < 0 or >= length throws IndexOutOfBoundsException

column5: Ch10
column6: the Gauss program filling int[101] via ia.length and summing it prints 5050

column5: Ch10,Ch10b
column6: an initializer's array length equals the expression count, initializers nest, a trailing comma is ignored, and indexing a null subarray element throws NullPointerException

column5: Ch10
column6: arrays have a public final `length`, implement Cloneable, and clone() returns a distinct array that is a shallow copy sharing subarrays

column5: Ch10
column6: getClass() on arrays of the same component type yields the same Class object named "[I" for int[], whose getSuperclass() is java.lang.Object

column2: An Array of Characters is Not a String
column5: Ch10
column6: char[] is not a String and is not NUL-terminated; String.toCharArray() returns a separate mutable array with the same characters

column5: Ch10
column6: ArrayStoreException on storing a supertype instance into an array whose actual element type is a subtype, while reads through the widened reference succeed
a VM-detected condition (e.g. integer divide by zero) throws at the specified expression/statement point, not an arbitrary one
a checked exception not named in the throws clause (incl. an overriding method widening throws, or a field/static initializer) is a compile-time error
Error and its subclasses need no throws clause: throwing one from an undeclared method compiles

column2: Why Runtime Exceptions are Not Checked
column6: RuntimeException and its subclasses need no throws clause: throwing one from an undeclared method compiles
the nearest dynamically-enclosing catch whose parameter type is the exception class or a superclass handles it; finally runs during propagation and its abrupt completion discards the original reason
side effects before the throw point are all visible and none after it are, even under optimization

column5: the only sources of an asynchronous exception are Thread.stop/ThreadGroup.stop (threads, absent on this target) and an InternalError raised by a VM/hardware fault; no Java construct can produce either, so the delay/precision rule has nothing to observe

column6: the worked program's exact output: ArithmeticException "/ by zero", NullPointerException, a user checked exception, and finally printing on every invocation
the hierarchy Object > Throwable > {Exception > RuntimeException, Error} is observable via catch and instanceof
catch (Exception e) catches every Exception, including any RuntimeException and any user subclass of Exception

each listed unchecked exception is thrown by its specific operation (zero divisor, bad covariant array store, bad cast, negative array size, null use, index out of range, bad numeric parse) and requires no throws clause
each listed checked exception (CloneNotSupportedException from clone on a non-Cloneable, ClassNotFoundException, InstantiationException, IOException and its subclasses) must be caught or declared
Error is a subclass of Throwable disjoint from Exception, so catch (Exception e) does not catch a thrown Error but catch (Throwable t) does
a static initializer or static-field initializer whose exception is not an Error surfaces as ExceptionInInitializerError
unbounded recursion throws StackOverflowError and an unsatisfiable allocation throws OutOfMemoryError, both catchable as VirtualMachineError/Error

column6: abrupt completion of an evaluated expression or substatement immediately aborts the enclosing statement with the same reason, and its succeeding steps do not run

column2: Hiding of Names by Local Variables
column6: a local hides a same-named field throughout its scope, and `this.x` still reaches the hidden field
declarators are initialized left to right, and a declarator's initializer runs only if the preceding one completed normally
a dangling `else` binds to the innermost `if` it could possibly belong to
the empty statement `;` does nothing and always completes normally
a labeled statement completes normally when its body completes abruptly via `break` with that label; a duplicate enclosing label is a compile error
an expression statement evaluates its expression and discards the value; only the listed expression forms are legal statements
the `if` condition must have type boolean — `if (1)` is a compile-time error
if-then executes the body when the condition is true and takes no action when false
if-then-else executes exactly one of the two branches according to the condition
switch on char/byte/short/int jumps to the matching case and falls through to following labels; unlabeled `break` exits; `default` runs when no case matches; duplicate case values are compile errors
while re-evaluates its boolean condition before each iteration, and executes the body zero times if the condition is false first
inside while, unlabeled break exits and continue restarts the loop; continue with label L re-loops only when the while carries L, else propagates
do-while always executes its body at least once, testing the condition after each iteration
inside do, unlabeled break exits and continue jumps to the condition evaluation; labeled continue re-tests only when the do carries that label
the do-loop toHexString implementation shown computes the same string as Integer.toHexString, emitting one digit for input 0
a for statement runs ForInit, then condition/body/ForUpdate repeatedly; the condition must be boolean
ForInit expressions evaluate left to right and stop at the first abrupt one; a ForInit declaration's scope covers the condition, update, and body
each iteration evaluates the condition, then the body, then ForUpdate left to right; an absent condition loops forever unless broken
in for, unlabeled break exits while continue still runs ForUpdate before the next iteration test
break transfers control out of the innermost switch/while/do/for or the named labeled statement, running intervening finally clauses innermost to outermost first
continue ends the current iteration of the innermost (or labeled) iteration statement, running intervening finally clauses first
return hands its evaluated value to the invoker as the method's value, after executing the finally clauses of enclosing try statements
throw transfers control to the nearest catch that can accept the value, running intervening finally clauses; a null throw operand and unhandled checked exceptions are observable

column6: A write is never lost: use/assign happen in program order and a read of a variable yields the most recently assigned value (field, array element, local) even across loops and calls.

An explicit implementation-latitude relaxation permitting early stores; its effect is visible only to a second, improperly synchronized thread.
Commentary on locking conventions and what the volatile rules amount to; contains no normative rule of its own.

Worked example requiring two threads calling to/fro concurrently to observe writes reordered; unreachable without threads.

Which HTML markers (<H1>-<H6>, <HR>) are reserved inside comment text — a formatting convention for the doc generator's output pages; no compiler or runtime behaviour depends on it.
Where the summary sentence ends (first period + blank/tab/terminator, or first tagline) — affects only the generated web page's prose; invisible to javelinac and javelina.
Defines '@' at line start as beginning a tagged paragraph and how far it extends; parsed only by the documentation processor, never by the language's lexer beyond comment skipping.
@see cross-reference syntax (Class#member, argument lists, <a href>) is resolved by the doc tool for hyperlinking; no name resolution or code generation consults it.
@author paragraph has 'no special internal structure' and may repeat — pure authorship metadata for generated pages, absent from compiler input semantics.
@version paragraph has no internal structure and is limited to at most one per comment — a doc-tool cardinality convention, not a compile-time or runtime rule.
@param naming and ordering conventions for method/constructor parameters are advisory ('the usual convention is'); parameter semantics come from the declaration, not the comment.
@return paragraph for non-void methods, at most one per comment — descriptive text for the generated page; the actual returned value is fixed by §14.16.
@exception names an exception class and its circumstances as free text; the checked-exception contract that a program can actually observe comes from the `throws` clause (§8.4.4), not this tag.

An illustrative listing of java.lang.Object source with its doc comments; the only behaviour it shows is Object's methods (specified in §20.1) and wait/notify monitor methods, which are excluded threads/locks on this target.

body is the single lead-in sentence "There are five problems with the grammar presented in preceding chapters" (p. 433), naming its subsections; it states no rule a program's compilation or execution can exhibit

column6: Object.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; a program can assert getClass()/getName(), the toString() "name@hex-hashCode" form, equals reflexivity/symmetry/null-false, the equals-implies-equal-hashCode contract, and clone()'s shallow copy vs CloneNotSupportedException. (wait/notify/finalize are thread/GC-latitude, but the section as a whole is observable.)

Cloneable.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; the marker is observable — Object.clone() on a non-Cloneable class throws CloneNotSupportedException, a Cloneable class gets a field-wise shallow copy, and arrays behave as Cloneable.

Class.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; known answers assertable: getName() == "java.lang.Object", array names "[Ljava.lang.Object;"/"[[[[[[[I", isInterface(), getSuperclass()==null for Object, getInterfaces() order matching the implements clause, toString() == "class "/"interface " + getName(), newInstance() and forName().

Boolean.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; known answers: TRUE/FALSE constants, Boolean("True") true vs Boolean("yes") false (case-insensitive, null-safe), toString/equals/hashCode/booleanValue and valueOf round-trips.

Character.java (+ CharacterData.java) present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE/MIN_RADIX/MAX_RADIX constants, the Unicode-attribute-table classifiers (isDefined/isLetter/isDigit/isUpperCase/isSpace...), toLowerCase/toUpperCase/toTitleCase mappings, and digit/forDigit radix round-trips are all known-answer assertable.

Number.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; the abstract contract is observable through its subclasses — a Number reference dispatching intValue/longValue/floatValue/doubleValue must yield the §5.1.2/§5.1.3 conversion of the wrapped value.

Integer.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE boundary constants, toString(i,radix) digit alphabet and '-' sign rule, toHexString/toOctalString/toBinaryString, parseInt/valueOf round-trips and NumberFormatException on bad input, equals/hashCode == the int value.

Long.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE boundaries, the specified hashCode == (int)(v^(v>>>32)), radix toString/parseLong/valueOf round-trips with NumberFormatException, and the intValue() §5.1.3 narrowing.

Float.java (+ FloatingDecimal/BinaryToASCIIBuffer) present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE/NaN/±INFINITY equal the stated intBitsToFloat bit patterns, floatToIntBits/intBitsToFloat round-trip, isNaN/isInfinite, and toString/valueOf string round-trips.

Double.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/; MIN_VALUE/MAX_VALUE/NaN/±INFINITY equal the stated longBitsToDouble bit patterns, doubleToLongBits/longBitsToDouble round-trip, isNaN/isInfinite, and toString/valueOf round-trips.

Math.java present in compiler/lib/java/lang/ (fdlibm transcendentals ported); E and PI constants, the enumerated NaN/±0/±infinity special cases for sin/cos/tan/asin/acos/atan/exp/log/sqrt/pow/IEEEremainder, and exact ceil/floor/rint/round/abs/min/max answers are all assertable.

String is implemented (compiler/lib/java/lang/String.java, 244 lines): known answers for length/charAt/indexOf/lastIndexOf/substring/concat/replace/trim/case-mapping, compareTo and equalsIgnoreCase orderings, valueOf round-trips for every primitive, boundary IndexOutOfBounds and NullPointerException, and intern() identity.

StringBuffer is implemented (compiler/lib/java/lang/StringBuffer.java, 131 lines): append/insert/reverse/setLength/setCharAt sequence results, capacity vs length invariant, getChars copy-out, and the specified IndexOutOfBounds/NegativeArraySize boundaries; also the target of + string concatenation.
ClassLoader is a 5-line stub; the class is implementable (defineClass/loadClass over the module registry) and is UNWRITTEN, not unobservable
Process has no source; reachable only via Runtime.exec, which is itself unwritten — an implementation gap, not an inapplicable one
Runtime has no source, yet gc/exit/totalMemory/freeMemory are all observable on this target — unwritten, not unobservable
SecurityManager is a 5-line stub; its check* methods are ordinary Java and observable — unwritten

System is implemented (compiler/lib/java/lang/System.java, 124 lines): arraycopy element results including self-overlap, ArrayStoreException on incompatible element kinds and the IndexOutOfBounds range checks; in/out/err stream identity and printed output; getProperty/getProperties/setProperties over the spec's key set; currentTimeMillis and exit status.

column5: Runnable exists to be handed to a Thread (§20.20). §17 threads are outside this target, so no program can ever run one — the interface is declarable but not observable.
§17 threads are outside this target (Java 1.0 minus synchronized; no threads in this embedding), so no program can create, start or join one.
A ThreadGroup groups Threads (§20.20), which this target has no way to create — §17 is outside the implemented language.

column2: The Class java.lang.Throwable and its Subclasses
column6: Throwable is implemented (compiler/lib/java/lang/Throwable.java) along with the full §20.22 exception/error hierarchy in compiler/lib/java/lang/: getMessage returning the saved string or null, toString's exact 'class-name: message' vs bare class-name form, printStackTrace writing that header to System.err or a given PrintStream, and the catch-by-supertype relationships of every listed predefined class.

ExceptionInInitializerError is implemented (compiler/lib/java/lang/ExceptionInInitializerError.java): getException returns the saved Throwable for the Throwable ctor and null for the no-arg and String ctors, getMessage is null for the Throwable ctor, and a failing static initializer (§12.4.2) makes it observable at a catch site.
Enumeration.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; a program can assert hasMoreElements/nextElement deliver every element in order and that nextElement past the end throws NoSuchElementException

BitSet.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; set/clear/get, growth on out-of-range set, negative index IndexOutOfBoundsException, and/or/xor results, the specified hashCode algorithm and the "{2, 4, 10}" toString form are all assertable

Date.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; getTime/setTime round-trip, UTC() known answers, field rollover (Jan 32 = Feb 1), before/after/equals/hashCode and the fixed-width toGMTString form are assertable

Dictionary.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; a program can subclass it and assert the abstract contract via Hashtable — size/isEmpty, put returning the previous element, remove returning the removed one, null key NullPointerException

Hashtable.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; put/get/remove/containsKey/contains known answers, size after rehash growth, clear, clone independence and keys()/elements() enumerations are assertable

Properties.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; getProperty defaults-chain lookup, propertyNames listing each key once, and load/save round-trip over the java.io byte-array streams (escapes, continuation lines, # comments) are assertable

Observable.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; addObserver/deleteObserver/countObservers, setChanged/hasChanged/clearChanged state and notifyObservers invoking update then clearing the mark are assertable — the spec states this mechanism is unrelated to threads
Observer.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; a program can implement it and assert update() receives the notifying Observable and the arg passed to notifyObservers

Random.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; the spec pins the exact LCG, so setSeed followed by nextInt/nextLong/nextFloat/nextDouble/nextGaussian yields a fixed known sequence that is assertable bit-for-bit

StringTokenizer.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; countTokens and the token sequence for default whitespace delimiters, an explicit delim set, returnTokens=true, and mid-stream nextToken(delim) are assertable

Vector.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; add/insert/remove index shifting, setSize null-fill, capacity/ensureCapacity/trimToSize growth rule, indexOf/lastIndexOf, copyInto, the "[a, b, c]" toString and IndexOutOfBounds/NoSuchElement throws are assertable
Stack.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; push/pop LIFO order, peek not removing, empty(), and search() returning 1-based distance from the top are assertable
EmptyStackException.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; a program can assert pop/peek on an empty Stack throws it, that it is catchable as RuntimeException, and that getMessage() is null

NoSuchElementException.java present in compiler/lib/java/util/; a program can assert Enumeration.nextElement past the end and Vector.firstElement on an empty Vector throw it, and that the (String) constructor's message is retrievable via getMessage

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/DataInput.java; via DataInputStream a program asserts the exact big-endian reconstruction formulas for readShort/UnsignedShort/Char/Int/Long/Float/Double, readBoolean/readByte sign rules, readLine's \\n \\r \\r\\n handling, readUTF's modified-UTF-8 decode, and EOFException on truncation.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/DataOutput.java; via DataOutputStream a program asserts the exact byte sequences written for each primitive width (writeShort/Int/Long/Float/Double), writeBytes low-byte vs writeChars two-byte, writeUTF length prefix + encoding, and round-trip back through DataInput.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/InputStream.java; a user subclass supplying only read() observes the layered defaults — read(b) == read(b,0,b.length), partial fills, -1 at end of file, skip's returned count, available()==0, markSupported()==false and reset() throwing IOException.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/FileInputStream.java (host fd via HostIO); a program writes a file then reads it back byte-exact, asserts -1 at EOF, getFD() identity, and FileNotFoundException on a nonexistent path.

column5: §22.5: a read blocks until another THREAD writes the pipe. With §17 outside this target the read can never be satisfied, so no program can observe the class.

column6: Present as compiler/lib/java/io/ByteArrayInputStream.java; a program asserts the pos/count arithmetic — read() returning buf[pos]&0xff then -1 at count, read(b,off,len) returning min(len,count-pos), skip's k, available()==count-pos, and reset() rewinding pos to 0 so offset-constructed bytes become readable.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/StringBufferInputStream.java; a program asserts that each byte is the low eight bits of the corresponding char (high bits discarded), plus available()==count-pos, skip, reset() to pos 0, and -1 at end.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/SequenceInputStream.java; a program asserts the logical concatenation order for both the (s1,s2) and Enumeration constructors, that each exhausted stream is closed before the next is read, and that -1 appears only after the last stream ends.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/FilterInputStream.java; with an instrumented inner stream a program asserts that every operation is a pure delegation to in (read/skip/available/close/mark/reset/markSupported) and that read(b) goes through read(b,0,b.length) rather than in.read(b).

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/BufferedInputStream.java; a program asserts markSupported()==true, that reset() after mark re-reads the identical byte sequence, that the buffered byte stream matches the unbuffered one exactly, available() >= buffered bytes, and IOException on reset() with no valid mark.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/DataInputStream.java; a program asserts the full DataInput contract over a wrapped stream — DataOutputStream round-trip for every primitive, readFully/skipBytes, static readUTF(DataInput), EOFException on a truncated value.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/LineNumberInputStream.java; a program asserts that \\r and \\r\\n are delivered as a single '\\n', getLineNumber()'s counting rule (0 while reading line one, 1 after its terminator), setLineNumber offsets, and mark/reset restoring the remembered line number.

Present as compiler/lib/java/io/PushbackInputStream.java; a program asserts that unread(b) makes the next read() (and the first byte of read(b,off,len)) return b, that a second unread throws IOException, available()==inner+1 while a byte is pushed back, and markSupported()==false.
StreamTokenizer has no source; it is pure Java over a stream, needs no thread and no host capability — purely unwritten

OutputStream.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a subclass implementing only write(int) can assert the specified defaults: write(b) == write(b,0,b.length), write(b,off,len) writes b[off]..b[off+len-1] one byte at a time in order, NPE on null b, IndexOutOfBoundsException on bad off/len, and flush()/close() returning silently.

FileOutputStream.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can write bytes to a host file and read them back through FileInputStream, assert the low-8-bits-only rule of write(int), getFD() identity, and FileNotFoundException for an unopenable path.

column5: The write half of the same pipe: it is only observable through a PipedInputStream read on another thread, and §17 is outside this target.

column6: ByteArrayOutputStream.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; fully in-memory, so a program can assert known answers for size(), reset(), toByteArray() contents and length, toString() zero-extension, toString(hibyte) == ((hibyte&0xff)<<8)|(buf[k]&0xff), and writeTo(this) doubling the buffer and terminating.

FilterOutputStream.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a recording OutputStream passed as `out` lets a program assert that each of write(int)/write(b)/write(b,off,len)/flush()/close() is forwarded verbatim to the contained stream.

BufferedOutputStream.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; with a recording sink a program can assert that bytes are held in buf until the buffer fills or flush() is called, that count stays in 0..buf.length, and that the sink finally receives exactly the bytes written in order.

DataOutputStream.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert exact big-endian byte encodings for writeShort/writeChar/writeInt/writeLong/writeFloat/writeDouble, the modified-UTF-8 form of writeUTF, and that size()/written advances by 1/2/4/8/len as specified — plus round-trip through DataInputStream.

PrintStream.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can capture the bytes into a ByteArrayOutputStream and assert the exact text of every print/println overload (including the four characters n,u,l,l for a null String), the '\\n' terminator, autoflush behaviour, NPE for a null char[], and that checkError() reports trouble instead of throwing IOException.

RandomAccessFile.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert seek/getFilePointer/length, that writes past the end extend the file, read() returning 0..255 then -1 at EOF, the DataInput/DataOutput round-trips, EOFException on a short read, IOException on writing an "r"-mode file, and IllegalArgumentException for a mode other than "r"/"rw".

File.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert the pure pathname rules (separatorChar '/', getName/getPath/getParent/getAbsolutePath/isAbsolute, the two- and three-arg constructors and their NPEs), equals by path, hashCode == getPath().hashCode() ^ 1234321, toString, and the host-backed exists/isFile/isDirectory/length/mkdir/mkdirs/renameTo/delete/list.

FilenameFilter.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can implement accept(File,String) and assert that File.list(filter) returns exactly the entries for which accept returned true, and that accept is called with the receiving File and the bare name.

FileDescriptor.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert that the in/out/err constants are non-null distinct descriptors, that valid() is true for an open FileOutputStream's getFD() and observe it after close().

IOException.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert getMessage() == null for the no-arg form, the saved string for IOException(String), that it is a checked Exception, and that catch(IOException) catches every one of its four specified subclasses.

EOFException.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert both constructors' getMessage() results, that it is caught as an IOException, and that DataInputStream/RandomAccessFile readers throw it when end of file arrives before the required bytes.

FileNotFoundException.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert both constructors' getMessage() results, catchability as IOException, and that new FileInputStream/FileOutputStream on a nonexistent path throws it.

InterruptedIOException.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can construct it and assert the specified public field bytesTransferred defaulting to 0, both constructors' getMessage() results, and that it is caught as an IOException — only the thread-interrupt trigger is unreachable on this target, not the class contract.

UTFDataFormatException.java present in compiler/lib/java/io/; a program can assert both constructors' getMessage() results, catchability as IOException, and that DataInputStream.readUTF over deliberately malformed modified-UTF-8 bytes throws it.
